- `GET /users/:id` — throws `ValidationError` for a non-integer ID and `NotFoundError` when the record is missing.
- `POST /users` — accumulates field errors into an array and throws a single `ValidationError` with all of them together, so clients get all problems in one response.

**404 catch-all middleware**
```js
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  next(new NotFoundError(`Route ${req.method} ${req.path} not found`));
});
```
Placed after all real routes, before the error handler. Unmatched requests flow here and are converted into a proper `NotFoundError` before going to the centralised handler.

**Centralised error handler (4-argument middleware)**
```js
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  if (err instanceof AppError) {
    return res.status(err.statusCode).json(err.toJSON());
  }
  // … fallback 500 for programmer errors
});
```
Express identifies a middleware as an error handler by its **exactly four arguments** `(err, req, res, next)`. The `instanceof AppError` branch handles all operational errors; anything else (e.g. a `TypeError` from a bug) hits the fallback, which logs the full stack internally but returns a safe, generic message to the client. The `eslint-disable-line` suppresses the "unused variable" warning on `next`, which must be present to satisfy Express's signature detection even though it isn't called.

**Guard on `app.listen`**
```js
if (require.main === module) { app.listen(...) }
```
Prevents the server from binding a port when the module is `require()`d in tests, so test files can import `app` cleanly without port conflicts.
